title: Deep Search for Molecular Oxygen in TW Hya
question: Is a significant amount of oxygen in TW Hya hiding in gas-phase O2, searched via 16O18O emission (plus SO and SO2)?

data.angular_resolution: 0.59'' by 0.50'', PA -88 deg (natural weighting); 30 to 35 au at 60.1 pc

what.value: Disk mass 2.5e-2 Msun and surface density profile (used for hydrogen budget)

evidence.quote: We adopt the (cite: Calahan2021) value of $2.5\times10^{-2}$ M$_\odot$ since it uses the HD line and multiple CO isotopologues to constrain the temperature structure.
Within 120 au, we use the surface density profile from (cite: Calahan2021)

what.value: Distance to TW Hya of 60.1 pc

evidence.quote: $D=60.1$ pc is the distance to TW Hya (cite: BailerJones2018)

what.value: Systemic velocity 2.86 km/s for the Keplerian mask

evidence.quote: We assumed a systemic velocity of 2.86 km s$^{-1}$ (cite: Favre2013)

what.value: Inclination 5.8 deg, position angle 151 deg and stellar mass 0.81 Msun for the Keplerian mask

evidence.quote: inclination $= 5.8\degree$, position angle $=151\degree$, and stellar mass $= 0.81$ M$_\odot$ (cite: Teague2019)

what.value: CO J=3-2 emission data for TW Hya used to build the Keplerian mask

evidence.quote: The mask was created using CO $J=3-2$ emission data for TW Hya from (cite: Huang2018)

what.value: Einstein A coefficient 1.33e-8 s^-1 and upper state energy 11.23 K for the 2_1-0_1 transition

evidence.quote: is the Einstein A coefficient of the $N_J=2_1-0_1$ transition (cite: Marechal1997)
11.23 K is the upper state energy (cite: Marechal1997)

what.value: Partition function Q(T) from the JPL catalog, 9.4 K to 300.0 K

evidence.quote: $Q(T)$ is the partition function from the JPL spectral line catalog (cite: Pickett1998; Mizushima1991; Crownover1990; Steinbach1975; Amano1974)

external_data.citation: Pickett et al. 1998 and others (cite: Pickett1998)

evidence.quote: we assumed a $^{16}$O$^{16}$O/$^{16}$O$^{18}$O ratio of 280 (cite: Taquet2018; Wilson1994)

external_data.citation: Taquet et al. 2018; Wilson & Rood 1994 (cite: Taquet2018; Wilson1994)

what.value: Molecular mass per hydrogen molecule of 2.8

evidence.quote: Assuming a molecular mass per hydrogen molecule of 2.8 (cite: Kauffman2008)

what.value: Molecular line data for SO and SO2 from LAMDA and CDMS

evidence.quote: using values from LAMDA (cite: Schoier2005) and CDMS (cite: Muller2001)

external_data.citation: Schoier et al. 2005 (cite: Schoier2005); Muller et al. 2001 (cite: Muller2001)

what.value: Earlier C15N 3-2 integrated fluxes in TW Hya of 150 +/- 20 and 160 +/- 13 mJy km/s

evidence.quote: They used two methods to calculate an integrated flux of $150 \pm 20$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ and $160 \pm 13$ mJy km s$^{-1}$

recipe.goal: Continuum subtraction and imaging of the 16O18O cube
recipe.method: uvcontsub (order 1) then tclean with natural weighting, with channel averaging and several Briggs robust and uvtaper combinations tried
key_parameters: natural weighting; channel width 0.078 km/s averaged to 0.235 km/s; rms 2.59 mJy/beam

recipe.goal: Keplerian-mask clean and disk-integrated flux limits in the image plane
recipe.method: Keplerian masks (120 au and 260 au) built from TW Hya parameters and CO J=3-2 data, used in tclean with a 5 sigma threshold; flux summed within 120 au and 260 au
assumptions: v_sys 2.86 km/s, distance 60.1 pc, inclination 5.8 deg, PA 151 deg, stellar mass 0.81 Msun

recipe.goal: Matched filtering in the visibility plane
recipe.method: cvel to correct for Earth's rotation, then Keplerian masks (120 au and 260 au) used as filters, Fourier transformed to a kernel and cross-correlated with the visibilities to give an impulse response spectrum; a 3 sigma response at 0 km/s would indicate emission
key_parameters: filters: Keplerian masks of 120 au and 260 au radius

recipe.goal: Convert flux limit to a limit on the number of O2 molecules
recipe.method: LTE single-line relation with the 1 sigma flux as F_l, over gas temperatures 9.4 K to 300.0 K, then scaled by 16O16O/16O18O = 280
key_parameters: A_20 = 1.33e-8 s^-1, nu = 233.94618 GHz, D = 60.1 pc, upper state energy 11.23 K, degeneracy 3
assumptions: LTE, temperature range 9.4 K to 300.0 K (set by the range of the JPL partition functions)

recipe.goal: Express the O2 limit as an abundance relative to H
recipe.method: Divide the O2 molecule limit by the number of hydrogen atoms from the Calahan et al. 2021 disk mass (whole disk) or surface density profile (within 120 au)
key_parameters: disk mass 2.5e-2 Msun (whole disk), 1.8e-2 Msun within 120 au; 2.1e55 and 1.5e55 H atoms
assumptions: Disk mass from Calahan et al. 2021; the paper notes a wide range of literature disk masses

recipe.goal: Search for SO, SO2 and C15N in the same data
recipe.method: Same imaging and matched filtering approach as for 16O18O; limits for SO and SO2 from the modified LTE equation; C15N found by matched filtering with the 120 au mask and measured in images
key_parameters: C15N images: Briggs robust = 2, uvtaper 0.3 arcsec, 200 au circular region

evidence.quote: We calculated a disk integrated flux (for a velocity range of 4.69 km s$^{-1}$) of $-11.8 \pm 14.2$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ within 120 au
and $7.4 \pm 18.0$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ within 260 au

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit on number of O2 molecules within 120 au (9.4-300 K)

evidence.quote: We obtained an upper limit of $(1.1-10.4)\times10^{49}$ O$_2$ molecules within 120 au

answer_key.quantity: Upper limit on number of O2 molecules within 260 au (9.4-300 K)

evidence.quote: and $(1.4-13.2)\times10^{49}$ molecules within 260 au, for a temperature range of 9.4 K to 300.0 K.

answer_key.quantity: Hydrogen atoms in the whole disk

evidence.quote: this equates to $2.1\times10^{55}$ hydrogen atoms in the whole disk.
to calculate a disk mass of $1.8\times10^{-2}$ M$_\odot$, which equates to $1.5\times10^{55}$ hydrogen atoms.
we estimate an O$_2$/H abundance of $(7.2-70)\times10^{-7}$ within 120 au
and $(6.4-62)\times10^{-7}$ within 260 au, for temperatures ranging from 9.4 K to 300.0 K.
The disk integrated flux for the SO line is $-0.05 \pm 12.5$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ within 120 au
and $-21.4 \pm 21.2$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ within 260 au (covering a range of 4.99 km s$^{-1}$)
For SO$_2$, the flux is $24.4 \pm 14.8$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ within 120 au
and $34.3 \pm 24.5$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ within 260 au (covering a range of 4.67 km s$^{-1}$)

answer_key.quantity: SO/H 1-sigma upper limit within 120 au and 260 au

evidence.quote: We calculate a 1$\sigma$ upper limit of SO/H = $(2.4-10)\times10^{-13}$ within 120 au and $(2.9-12)\times10^{-13}$ within 260 au

answer_key.quantity: SO2/H 1-sigma upper limit within 120 au and 260 au

evidence.quote: SO$_2$/H = $(7.9-197)\times10^{-13}$ within 120 au and $(9.1-229)\times10^{-13}$ within 260 au, for a temperature range of 9.4 K to 300.0 K.
Using matched filtering with the 120 au Keplerian mask, we obtained a 7$\sigma$ filter response.

answer_key.quantity: C15N integrated flux (2.33 km/s range, 200 au region)

evidence.quote: with an integrated flux of $113.5 \pm 17.0$ mJy km s$^{-1}$ for a range of 2.33 km s$^{-1}$, calculated within a 200 au circular region covering visible emission.

rediscovery_reason: Single named ALMA project and stated numeric limits; imaging and the LTE abundance calculation are reproducible within tolerance, though public release of the data is not stated in the paper
